title: Citizenship granted to Iranian soccer players who sought asylum

By Ned Hammond

Topic:Human Rights

Two former Iranian national soccer players have been sworn in as Australian citizens at a ceremony in Brisbane. (Supplied)

Two Iranian national women's soccer team members who sought asylum in Australia in March have been granted citizenship.

Fatemeh Pasandideh and Atefeh Ramezanisadeh were sworn in as Australian citizens by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke in a ceremony in Brisbane on Wednesday.

The Human Rights Law Centre is urging the government to offer the same pathway to refugees who have been living in Australia for years.

Two Iranian women's soccer team players who sought asylum in Australia after competing in the Asian Cup have been granted citizenship.

Iran competed in Australia in March as war broke out in the Middle East after a US-Israel attack on the Islamic Republic.

Concerns were raised about the national team's safety after the players refused to sing the Iranian national anthem ahead of their game against South Korea and were criticised on Iranian state television.

Seven team members, including a handler, were granted humanitarian visas to remain in Australia, but five withdrew their claims and returned to Iran.

Concerns were raised over the potential for the players to face retribution from the Iranian government when returning home. (AAP: Russell Freeman)

The two remaining players, Fatemeh Pasandideh and Atefeh Ramezanisadeh, were granted citizenship on Wednesday.

Ms Pasandideh and Ms Ramezanisadeh were sworn in as citizens by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke at a ceremony in Brisbane.

The women were sworn in by Minister for Home Affairs Tony Burke. (Supplied)

They were accompanied by members of the local Iranian community, with friends and supporters celebrating the occasion.

Ms Pasandideh said it was "one of the happiest days of my life".

"After everything we've been through and all the challenges we faced, this moment means more than words can express," she said.

"Thank you, Australia, for giving me this opportunity. I'm honoured to be part of this nation."

The two women said the ceremony and their citizenship "meant a great deal to us". (Supplied)

Ms Ramezanisadeh said she was "deeply proud to become an Australian citizen".

"Australia has given me the opportunity to build my life and my future, and I feel, more than ever, that I belong here," she said.

Associate legal director at the Human Rights Law Centre (HRLC) Laura John urged the government to extend the same pathway to citizenship to Iranians formerly in offshore detention who have been living in Australia for years.

She said the HRLC understood that about 700 refugees have lived in the Australian community for more than a decade on "short-term, insecure bridging visas".

The remaining members of Iran's women's football team might have left Australia, but the journey is far from over, as members of the Iranian-Australian community share what really went into the fight to protect their countrywomen.

"Almost most half are from Iran and cannot return there," Ms John said.

"Many have close family members, including children and spouses, who are Australian citizens or permanent residents."

She said HRLC clients Fatemeh Lahmidi and Mahsa Mazaheri have been in Australia for more than 13 years and have not yet been granted citizenship.

Ms Lahmidi, who is a mother, aged care worker and refugee from Iran, said she was happy for the soccer players but felt "heartbroken" she was unable to obtain citizenship.

"My family has been waiting for so many years, and it's hard to understand why we are still living with so much uncertainty while others receive citizenship so quickly," she said.

"Australia is the only home my children really know.

Small business owner Ms Mazaheri said her daughters and husband were Australian citizens and that the country had been her home for more than 10 years.

"It is painful to see the difference in how some people are treated while many others, like us, remain in uncertainty for so many years," she said.
